conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 62 years old and female. I'm here because I had another heart attack recently and they put in another stent. It was really scary, I thought I was doing okay after my last one, but then the chest pain came back and it wouldn't go away.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please tell me when you first started experiencing the chest pain and how it has been progressing since your last stent placement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I guess it started maybe a couple of weeks ago, and it was just like the last time—really intense, like a crushing pain in my chest. It didn’t go away, so I had to go to the ER. It was really frightening, honestly.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe any factors that make the chest pain better or worse, such as physical activity, rest, or certain foods? Also, have you been adhering to your prescribed medications since your last stent placement?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The chest pain was really bad, like the last time, and it didn’t get better with rest or anything. I’ve been taking my medications as prescribed, though. I know it’s important, so I haven’t missed any doses.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you describe any other symptoms you experienced along with the chest pain, such as shortness of breath, dizziness, nausea, or sweating? Also, have you noticed any changes in your activity level or any new symptoms since the chest pain began?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I didn't have any shortness of breath or dizziness with the chest pain, but I did notice my legs have been a little swollen since I came home from the hospital. I’ve been walking my dog every day, though, so I haven’t been completely inactive. I just feel like I need to be careful and not push myself too hard.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please describe the swelling in your legs in more detail, such as when it started, whether it is worse in one leg than the other, and if you have noticed any changes in the swelling over time?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The swelling started after I came home from the hospital, and it's been pretty consistent since then. It's worse in my right leg, and I've noticed it's a bit pitting when I press on it. It doesn't really get better throughout the day, and I've had to use a couple of pillows to sleep more comfortably at night.
